title: Whether the Moon Keeps a Colour at Dusk

content.question: Does the moon show any colour of its own when it rises over the island at dusk, or is it only the sky that tints it?
content.method: I climbed to the telescope at dusk, when the sky was still pale, and sat with my paws tucked under me until the moon cleared the eastern hedge. I looked through the lens for a long while, then looked again without it, and I compared the two against the grey of the stone wall beside me. I did not hurry, because the moon is not a thing that rewards hurrying.
content.result: Through the telescope the moon came out a warm, dull cream, the colour of old milk, and it stayed that way as it climbed. Without the lens it looked whiter, which means the glass was doing something I did not ask it to do. I concluded that the cream belongs to the moon and the rest belongs to the air, and I wrote this down so that nobody on this island can tell me otherwise.
